narrative.overview:
Projammr is a dim room built around the record that is playing. The cover art is the only light source: blurred into the masthead, thrown across the page as a faint wash, tinting the player and the share page, and moving with the audio on the now-playing sheet. Everything else is the room's furniture: true-neutral paper and ink, fine grain, glass, and hairlines. It sits back so the music carries the page.

The furniture is precise. Data is set in a monospace face, labels are tracked caps in a pixel mono, and readouts behave like studio gear: a loudness meter with a caret and a dotted reference line, a status dot that fills like a pie, a waveform of square bars. The gear is modern and professional, never literal hardware. It feels warm rather than clinical because the display face is a halftone serif, the page carries grain, and the art drifts slowly behind the title.

Boldness is spent in one place per page (the masthead on entity pages, the art field on the share page and the now-playing sheet); every other surface is quieter than stock shadcn. Structure encodes information: a rule, a heading, a chip or a badge appears because it says something.
keyCharacteristics: Artwork is the only source of hue; with no artwork the room is pure grayscale.
True-neutral paper and ink with a wide range, in light and dark themes.
Four self-hosted faces, each with exactly one job; monospace is the document default.
Flat pages; depth comes from blurred art, the wash, grain and glass. Only overlays lift.
Studio-gear readouts (meters, carets, ticks, pies, waveforms) instead of charts and cards.
One orchestrated page-load reveal; ambient motion only where the art lives; everything respects `prefers-reduced-motion`.
One language across the client, dit, the share page and the public website.

rules.name: The Borrowed Light Rule
rules.body: There is no brand hue. A page with no artwork anywhere in its fallback chain is pure grayscale. The only non-artwork colours are user status and label colours, `--warn` and `--danger`.

rules.name: The No Success Colour Rule
rules.body: There is deliberately no green. Confirm actions are ink or art; a diff is not a warning, so it never uses `--warn` or `--danger`.

rules.name: The Spine Names Rule
rules.body: New code uses the spine names directly (`text-ink-soft`, not `text-muted-foreground`). The shadcn aliases exist for the library, not for us.

rules.name: The Server Extracts Rule
rules.body: Never compute the page accent from pixels in the browser. The one exception is the now-playing lava field, where `lib/cover-palette.ts` samples several distinct colours from the cover on a small canvas, because the server stores one accent and the field needs a handful.

rules.name: The One Job Rule
rules.body: Each face has exactly one job. Redaction 35 is only the page `<h1>`; Departure Mono is only labels, always tracked caps and never prose; Spline Sans Mono is everything else.

rules.name: The Scale Only Rule
rules.body: Use `text-micro`, `text-small`, `text-body`, `text-lead`, `text-section`, `text-subtitle`, `text-title` and `text-display`. Never `text-xs`, `text-sm`, `text-lg` or arbitrary `text-[…]` sizes; `text-micro` is the floor.

rules.name: The Centred Measure Rule
rules.body: Content sits in a centred, capped column; wide screens frame the page with margin rather than anchoring everything to the left edge. Only tables and settings panes opt out with `PAGE_WIDE`.

rules.name: The One Phone Tier Rule
rules.body: Say `stack:` or `phone:`, never a raw `max-[…px]:` width, and never build a band that is half phone, half desktop.

rules.name: The Flat Room Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. No shadow on cards, rows, buttons, sections or the rail; only overlays lift, and only with the overlay values.

rules.name: The Light, Not Bitmap Rule
rules.body: The page wash is built from the extracted accent as gradients. Never blur the cover bitmap across the page: it leaves a dark block.

rules.name: The Single Seam Rule
rules.body: Art and scrim end at the same edge, and the art's mask reaches zero before that edge, or the artwork reappears below the fold as a hard band.

rules.name: The Line Not Box Rule
rules.body: If a group needs separating, use a heading or a hairline. A border that fully encloses content is reserved for overlays and inputs.

rules.name: The One Cover Per Band Rule
rules.body: A band is lit by one cover, and its light fades out before both edges, so two hues never share a band or meet on a line between bands. A relight swaps the band's light for another; it never adds a second.

rules.name: The Real Gear Rule
rules.body: A marketing page proves a claim with the app's own gear rendered to HTML over the demo catalogue, or a screenshot of it. Every raster the site ships is one of the four covers or one of those screenshots, its source recorded in `apps/web/CLAUDE.md`: no mockups, illustrations or browser frames.

dos: **Do** use the spine tokens (`text-ink-soft`, `bg-paper-sunk`, `border-rule`) and the type scale (`text-micro` through `text-display`).
**Do** put anything label-shaped in `font-sub` tracked caps via `LABEL`, `EYEBROW`, `RailLabel` or `SectionHead`.
**Do** read artwork through `--art`, `--art-glow` and `--art-image`, and carry it with `ArtProvider`, `ArtSwatch` or `artVarsFromAccent`.
**Do** reuse the primitives in `packages/ui` and `apps/client/src/components/` before writing a new surface.
**Do** keep server components server: `SectionHead`, `RailBlock`, `Rows`, `MetadataItem`, `Masthead` and `PageHead` have no `"use client"`.
**Do** make hover-revealed affordances also focus-revealed (`group-focus-within:opacity-100`) and put hover-only affordances behind `fine:`.
**Do** draw quantities as studio readouts (meters, ticks, carets, pies, waveforms) rather than charts in cards.
**Do** use `motion-ink`/`motion-reveal`/`motion-move`/`motion-settle` on stateless primitives and `m` with `SPRING`/`FADE`/`LEAVE` everywhere React owns the state.
**Do** meet WCAG 2.2 AA: contrast on every theme and over art (`.on-art`), visible focus, and 44px touch targets.
**Do** render gear on a marketing page from `@workspace/ui` with no `client:` directive, add its file to `site.css`'s `@source` lines, and keep the page's motion in CSS.
donts: **Don't** use `text-xs`, `text-sm`, `text-lg` or arbitrary `text-[…]` sizes; shadcn colour names in new code; Tailwind palette hues (`green-600`, `sky-500`, `bg-black/50`); `#hex`, `rgb()` or `oklch()` literals in components; or raw `max-[…px]:` widths where `stack:` or `phone:` says it.
**Don't** use `Separator` stacks, bordered cards, `shadow-lg`, or `rounded-lg` panels as section containers.
**Don't** build a generic SaaS dashboard: cards in grids, KPI tiles, brand-blue buttons, rounded shadowed panels.
**Don't** go skeuomorphic: literal knobs, brushed metal, fake LEDs or screws. The gear is modern, not a DAW skin.
**Don't** imitate a streaming app: green accents, huge rounded art tiles, carousel shelves.
**Don't** use the neon "producer" look: purple gradients, glow, synthwave.
**Don't** use filled or circular play buttons, or hover backgrounds on icon buttons.

**Don't** add hover lifts, bounce, or a literal duration or stiffness at a call site; don't animate blur, `width`, `height` or `left` on anything larger than a control or a collapsible panel; don't put Motion on a named view-transition boundary.
**Don't** blur the cover bitmap for the page wash.
**Don't** set `--art` inline; set the `--art-light` and `--art-dark` pairs.
**Don't** nest a `<button>` inside an anchor or a `role="button"`.
